routes.label: Update the number of apples after each sale

question: Jack had a bag of \(128\) apples. He sold \(25\%\) of them to Jill. Next he sold \(25\%\) of those remaining to June. Of those apples still in his bag, he gave the shiniest one to his teacher. How many apples did Jack have then?
solution:
Since \(25\%=\frac14\), Jill buys \(\frac14\times128=32\) apples, leaving \(128-32=96\). June’s purchase is one quarter of these remaining \(96\) apples, so she buys \(\frac14\times96=24\), leaving \(96-24=72\). After Jack gives his teacher one apple, he has
\[
72-1=71
\]
apples. The answer is \(71\), choice D.
